observation_summary: The FastDateFormat 'z' pattern (timezone name) always prints the system default timezone instead of the timezone associated with the Calendar instance passed to the format() method.
hypothesis: The TimeZoneNameRule class was incorrectly using a cached TimeZone instance (the one associated with the FastDateFormat instance) instead of dynamically retrieving the TimeZone from the Calendar object provided during the formatting process.
prediction: The code will be modified to remove the cached TimeZone field in TimeZoneNameRule and instead retrieve the TimeZone from the Calendar object inside the appendTo() method.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows the removal of the 'zone' field from the TimeZoneNameRule class and the addition of 'TimeZone zone = calendar.getTimeZone();' inside the appendTo() method, confirming that the logic was changed to use the Calendar's timezone dynamically.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an incorrect computational strategy where the code used a static, pre-configured timezone instead of the dynamic timezone provided by the input Calendar object. This is a procedural logic error within the formatting method, making it an Algorithm/Method defect.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'TimeZoneNameRule class stopped respecting the Calendar instance's timezone, and instead now always uses the mTimeZone of the FastDateFormat instance itself'
The fix diff shows the removal of 'private final TimeZone zone;' from the class fields.
The fix diff shows the addition of 'TimeZone zone = calendar.getTimeZone();' inside the 'appendTo' method.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a field was removed, the core issue is the procedural logic of how the timezone is retrieved and used during the formatting process, not just an incorrect initial value.
